transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-08 14:30 UTC | Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Alex Turner, Samira Shah, Liam O'Neill (Redwood); Priya Kapoor, Marcus Li, Daniel Weber, Anna Santos (Peregrine)

Summary (auto): Walkthrough of outstanding legal redlines, DPA clause concerns, SLA expectations, and pricing path. Technical clarifications around KMS, VPC, and data residency.

00:00 Alex (AE): hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood inference, i'm joined by samira our solutions eng and liam from customer success. how's everyone doing today?
00:12 Priya (Legal): hey, good, thanks. we have about an hour set aside. want to focus on the redlines and the pricing ask we saw in the RFP.
00:20 Marcus (Procurement): yes and i need to understand the commit levels and any egress fees, also curious about private deployment options.
00:31 Samira (SE): quick note — when we say private deployment here, we mean the private plane control plane plus customer-managed VPC or on-prem option; sorry our docs sometimes say "Redwood Privates" which is a stale name from early drafts.
00:45 Daniel (Security): that's fine, just confirm key management options — can we bring our KMS? we need HSM-backed keys for production.
00:53 Samira (SE): yep, we support customer-managed KMS via standard KMS integrations and also an on-prem HSM option for the private runtime. in practice the flow is: request-> routed to customer VPC endpoint -> model inference runs with your key wrapping the secrets. i'll share the vpc diagram.
01:12 Priya (Legal): on the MSA we marked three items: data residency, liability cap, and DPA subprocessor list. liability cap is a big ask for us because of financial regs. your standard is 1x ARR in the draft, we're asking for clarification and a carveout for gross negligence.
01:30 Alex (AE): understood. historically we try to keep liability aligned with commit level; for enterprise we can discuss higher caps or insurance-backed options. we'll annotate in the redline the gross negligence carveout language.
01:44 Marcus (Procurement): about pricing — the spreadsheet suggested a 12-month commit with burst credits. how strict is the commit meter? are there true overage rates?
01:55 Liam (CSM): commits are flexible — the committed capacity gives you a discounted unit price and burst is available at a slightly higher rate. we do have overage rates, but for pilot we can set a provisional cushion.
02:10 Anna (Privacy): we also need data deletion SLAs — how long logs live, where embedding vectors land, are embeddings considered customer data?
02:22 Samira (SE): embeddings are stored only if you opt in to the vector store add-on; by default we don't persist call-level embeddings. audit logs and minimal telemetry for debugging are retained per the DPA, and we can map retention windows. i'll include exact retention times in the doc.
02:40 Priya (Legal): DPA — subprocessor list is currently missing an item. can you confirm all cloud providers and any third-party monitoring vendors?
02:50 Alex (AE): sure — primary infra is G-Cloud us-east and eu-west through our provider partners; we'll enumerate them in the DPA. any monitoring vendors — we use a hosted tracing provider but can provide SOC reports.
03:05 Marcus (Procurement): can we talk about SLA? Peregrine requires 99.9% uptime for production endpoints and a 200ms p95 latency target for the inference calls on the dedicated tier. can you commit to that?
03:22 Samira (SE): we have SLA tiers. 99.9% is in our enterprise SLA for dedicated capacity; latency guarantees depend heavily on model selection and sequence length. the 200ms p95 is achievable for smaller models and optimized kernels — for larger LLMs it's higher. we can define a performance SLO for your pilot load.
03:40 Daniel (Security): and in the SLA, is there a credit structure? what's the remedy?
03:46 Alex (AE): yes credits scale by downtime and are detailed in the SLA schedule — we'll share the schedule. legal can review options if they prefer monetary credits vs. service remediation.
04:00 Priya (Legal): another legal note: we asked for audit rights in the DPA for our in-house auditors — remote review and periodic audit. any constraints?
04:12 Liam (CSM): we allow audit rights but typically with notice and using redacted logs; for private deployments we can be more flexible. we'll outline the audit process.
04:28 Marcus (Procurement): i'm hearing there are two procurement paths: quick pilot under standard terms and a full enterprise MSA afterwards. what is the expected timeline to go from pilot to full contracting?
04:40 Alex (AE): typical timeline is pilot 2-4 weeks to validate technical fit, then legal finalizes the MSA which can take 2-6 weeks depending on redlines. we want to lock pricing and commit during the pilot to speed enterprise rollout.
04:55 Priya (Legal): risk team will want SOC2 and pen test results; do you have a recent report?
05:03 Samira (SE): we have a SOC2 type II report from 2025 and a third-party pentest summary — i'll attach sanitized versions.
05:15 Daniel (Security): for KMS, can you support key rotation and split-key policies? we require rotation every 90 days and the ability to revoke keys remotely.
05:26 Samira (SE): yes, rotation is supported via the KMS provider, and in private mode you control rotation and revocation. we'll note the operational steps.
05:40 Alex (AE): ok back to pricing — Marcus, can you share internal thresholds for the approver? volume bands, commit size?
05:48 Marcus (Procurement): we need to know the baseline QPS and token volume estimate; finance is sensitive to monthly OpEx vs CapEx. prefer commit that maps to predictable spend.
05:59 Samira (SE): if you share sample traffic we can produce a cost model; we also recommend quantization and batching settings to hit cost targets.
06:10 Anna (Privacy): regarding international traffic — if we have EU-only data, can that stay in eu-west region?
06:18 Samira (SE): yes you can pin region routing for residency, we'll include region routing rules in the DPA/ops doc.
06:30 Priya (Legal): about indemnity — we asked for a stronger IP indemnity clause around generated outputs. can we get a standard carveout?
06:40 Alex (AE): we provide a reasonable indemnity for third-party IP claims if caused by the model outputs under certain usage bounds. i'll work with legal to draft clearer language.
06:55 Marcus (Procurement): one practical question — are there any data egress fees if we route logs to our SIEM in another region?
07:03 Samira (SE): egress fees may apply depending on cross-region transfer and cloud provider bills; we'll enumerate expected egress tiers in the pricing sheet.
07:20 Daniel (Security): onboarding checklist — we need SSO/SAML, RBAC mapping, and the ability to restrict endpoints by subnet.
07:30 Liam (CSM): all supported — we'll include SSO integration docs and a template RBAC mapping.
07:40 Priya (Legal): ok let's make sure action items are explicit. we need the redline MSA, DPA with subprocessors, SOC2 report, KMS flow, and a pilot pricing spreadsheet.
07:52 Alex (AE): agreed, we'll deliver those. any blockers to starting the pilot while legal continues review?
08:00 Marcus (Procurement): procurement will need a signed NDA and an internal PO for pilot spending. timeline dependent on finance, but aim is to get PO in two weeks.
08:12 Alex (AE): we can accept an NDA and a pilot PO; we'll also give a limited test account for the pilot.
08:20 Samira (SE): quick technical scope for the pilot — three endpoints: low-latency generation, embeddings for search, and a reranking route. we recommend dedicated small pool for consistent perf.
08:35 Daniel (Security): for the pilot data set we'll use redacted production subsets; ensure logs are segmented and tagged.
08:45 Samira (SE): noted. we'll provide log tagging guidance.
08:53 Priya (Legal): one more DPA note — breach notification windows. we asked for 24 hours. is that feasible?
09:01 Alex (AE): our standard is 72 hours for incident classification, but for privileged customers we can commit to 48 hours; 24 is challenging operationally but i'll flag it to ops/legal for discussion.
09:16 Marcus (Procurement): if 24 isn't feasible, we need explicit escalation matrix.
09:22 Liam (CSM): we'll provide an escalation matrix with SLAs for incident types.
09:30 Priya (Legal): ok let's recap next steps.
09:33 Alex (AE): recap: we'll send the MSA redline and DPA with full subprocessors, attach SOC2 and pentest summary, provide KMS/VPC diagram and the pilot pricing spreadsheet. Marcus will route pricing to finance. target internal approval ~3 weeks.
09:50 Marcus (Procurement): yes, i'll aim to have finance feedback by 2026-09-29.
09:58 Priya (Legal): legal will review redlines and give top-3 must-haves.
10:05 Alex (AE): perfect. any other questions?
10:12 Daniel (Security): can you confirm support window for on-call during pilot? we may need an SRE contact.
10:20 Samira (SE): we can provide a named SRE for the pilot and weekly syncs.
10:26 Liam (CSM): i'll set up the pilot calendar invite after we circulate docs.
10:34 Alex (AE): thanks all. we'll aim to get the docs out by Friday. appreciate the time.
10:40 Priya (Legal): thanks. talk soon.

(occasional crosstalk, mis-transcriptions: "Redwood privates" vs "private plane", "G-Cloud" transcribed from "GCP", some filler words and partial speaker attribution mismatches appear.)
